# Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead · LinkedIn · 2026-10-22T00:00:00+00:00

**Lindstead**.

---

Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs.

On-demand price of one H100 per hour, September to October:
• Nebius (NL): €3.38 to €3.95, up 17%
• Scaleway (FR): €2.73 to €2.87, up 5%
• Verda (FI): €3.09 to €3.18, up 3%

Nebius raised its newest GPUs most. A B300 now costs €8.33 an hour, up 21 percent. OVHcloud and Hetzner did not change their prices.

MSP Business and Dutch IT Channel reported the Nebius increase on 30 September, citing the index.

Every change per provider and GPU, in the October edition:
https://lnkd.in/ehRtYBk4

results.title: gpueuro #3: Verda raises prices 3 times in a week
results.author: Gunars Mie
highlights:
Gunars Mie

Oct 26, 2026

Prices checked 26 Oct 2026. On-demand, per GPU-hour, ex-VAT.

Verda raised its on-demand prices 3 times in one week. Our daily checks of Verda’s EUR price page found steps on 21, 24 and 25 Oct. The H100 went from €3.82 to €4.07 (+6.5%). That makes Verda’s H100 the most expensive of the six we rank, at more than double Seeweb’s €1.89.

Source: https://verda.com/pricing 

H100 ranking, cheapest first:

- Seeweb €1.89
- Gcore €2.73 (bare metal; virtual €2.82)
- OVHcloud €2.80
- Scaleway €2.87 (approx.)
- Nebius €4.02 ($4.50)
- Verda €4.07

Verda’s other moves (19 → 26 Oct):

- H200: €4.98 → €5.31
- B200: €7.14 → €7.54
- B300: €9.05 → €9.65
- GB300: €10.40 → €11.10
- A100 80GB: €1.83 → €1.92
- L40S: €1.56 → €1.61

Nebius’s dollar prices didn’t change. Its euro prices only moved with the ECB rate (1.1193 on 23 Oct): H100 €4.00 → €4.02. Nothing else in the table changed.

Source: https://docs.nebius.com/compute/resources/pricing

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU list prices up to 21% while H100 spot sits at $0.79 - CTOL Digital Solutions
highlights:
Posted prices for four Nebius GPU types rose 17 to 21 percent on 1 October. Its own spot board shows Blackwell chips near 60 percent of list and an H100 at the floor, so the squeeze sits in particular chips and regions.

Nebius told CNBC this week that AI computing prices are rising faster than it expected. On 1 October it lifted the posted price of four GPU types by 17 to 21 percent.

...

The Nebius pricing documentation dates two changes. The first took effect on 1 October, when on demand prices per GPU hour rose for four chips. Reuters reported on 17 September that Nebius had announced it, its second price rise in three months.

- B300 went from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21.0 percent, the largest rise.
- B200 went from $7.15 to $8.50, up 18.9 percent.
- H200 went from $4.50 to $5.40, up 20.0 percent.
- H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9 percent, the smallest rise of the four.

The RTX PRO 6000 stayed at $1.80, so the rise did not reach every GPU.

The second change came on 8 October. The preemptible tier, which rents interruptible capacity at a discount, stopped using fixed prices. It moved to dynamic spot pricing that can change every 15 minutes.

One rule in the documentation matters most. The highest spot price is always one cent below the current on demand rate, so the new list price is a ceiling. The floor is $0.79 or $0.99 depending on the chip. The posted price rise matters to a spot buyer only when the market pushes against that ceiling.

results.title: Nebius brings compute pricing into the open as Europe’s AI builders scale on its cloud
highlights:
October 21, 2026

- Introduces public live prices for GPU spot capacity to expand transparent and flexible access to AI compute
- Expands AI Builder Program to Europe with NVIDIA to accelerate European AI development
- Across countries and industries, Europe’s most ambitious AI companies are building on Nebius

BERLIN — NVIDIA GTC, October 21, 2026 — Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS), the AI cloud company, today announced public live spot pricing for GPU compute, giving teams greater visibility and control over their compute costs.

AI teams are increasingly experimenting, training and running production services at the same time. Each calls for a different way to access and use compute capacity. Nebius is expanding its portfolio of pricing mechanisms to meet these needs, as part of its vision to promote an open market for compute.

Alongside live preemptible spot pricing, reserve auctions offer defined capacity blocks for short-term compute needs, while pay-as-you-go enables access to compute on demand without a fixed-term reservation. Nebius is also piloting a capacity-rebate program that enables customers to recover value by releasing idle GPUs back into the spot capacity pool.

...

Nebius is working with the ecosystem to make live pricing more widely available. Public live pricing for Spot PVMs is available now at nebius.com/spot-prices and on Shadeform, Silicon Data and GPU Finder.
